intro: IEC 61400-25 is IEC 61850 for wind power plants. It adds logical nodes for the turbine, its rotor, generator and converter, the weather, and the control of the whole park. IEC 61400-25-4 maps the model onto protocols; with the MMS mapping, a turbine talks like any IEC 61850 server.

associate.title: Associate
associate.text: The park controller opens TCP port 102 on turbine WT01 and sets up an MMS association. With the MMS mapping, a turbine is an ordinary IEC 61850 server.

read.title: Read the turbine
read.text: One Read asks for three values: active power in WTUR1, rotor speed in WROT1 and wind speed in WMET1. WTUR also holds the turbine's operating state, TurSt.

subscribe.title: Ask for reports
subscribe.text: The controller enables report urcbWTG01. The turbine now sends its data set when a value changes, and every 10 s in any case.

limit.title: A limit for the park
limit.text: The grid operator's SCADA operates WAPC1, the park's active power control: at most 5.4 MW for the whole plant.

follow.title: Turbines follow
follow.text: The park controller gives each of the three turbines its share: 1800 kW. WT01 pitches its blades, ramps down and reports its new power.

frames.initiate-req: Let's talk MMS: my sizes and services
frames.read-req: Your power, rotor speed and wind speed?
frames.oper: The park may export 5.4 MW at most

notes.initiate-req: First TCP to port 102 and a COTP connection, as in the IEC 61850 MMS lesson. Then the MMS Initiate offers sizes and services.
notes.initiate-resp: The turbine answers with its own sizes and services. Its model can now be browsed, or read from its SCL file.
notes.oper: A control on WAPC, the logical node for the park's active power: a new reference value for the plant's output. The park controller answers with a Write response.
notes.share: How the limit reaches each turbine is up to the park controller. Inside the park, many use the turbine maker's own protocol for this.
notes.report: An unsolicited InformationReport from urcbWTG01 with W, RotSpd and HorWdSpd. Its reason code says what triggered it: a data change.

tpkt-143.name: TPKT
tpkt-143.note: Version 3, then the length of the whole message: 0x008F = 143 bytes.

cotp-dt.name: COTP
cotp-dt.note: A data unit (0xF0), the last of its message (0x80).

session.name: Session
session.note: Two short session headers: give tokens, data transfer.

presentation.name: Presentation
presentation.note: Fully encoded data, presentation context 3: what follows is MMS.

presentation-long.name: Presentation
presentation-long.note: Fully encoded data, context 3: MMS follows. 81 81 is a long length: 0x81 says one length byte follows, and that byte, 0x81, is 129.

confirmed-req.name: Confirmed request
confirmed-req.note: Tag A0: a request that expects an answer. The next byte counts the bytes inside it.

confirmed-resp.name: Confirmed response
confirmed-resp.note: Tag A1: the answer to a request.

invoke-3.name: Invoke ID 3
invoke-3.note: A number the controller picks. The answer carries the same one.

invoke-3-resp.name: Invoke ID 3
invoke-3-resp.note: The same number as the request: this answers it.

invoke-4.name: Invoke ID 4
invoke-4.note: A new request, a new number.

invoke-4-resp.name: Invoke ID 4
invoke-4-resp.note: This answers the write to RptEna.

spec.name: Variable list
spec.note: A list of variables, each given by its name. Here there are three.

var.name: Variable
var.note: One entry of the list. Its name follows.

domain-specific.name: Domain-specific name
domain-specific.note: A name in two parts: the domain and the item.

domain.name: Domain
domain.note: "WT01WTG": the logical device WTG of the IED WT01.

item-wdspd.name: Item
item-wdspd.note: "WMET1$MX$HorWdSpd$mag$f": the horizontal wind speed, from the anemometer on the nacelle.

results.name: Results
results.note: Three results, in the order they were asked for.

float-tag.name: Floating point
float-tag.note: Tag 0x87 (a float), 5 bytes. 08: an IEEE 754 single-precision float follows.

w.name: W
w.note: 2350.0. The unit, kW, is in the attribute units (CF).

write-spec.name: Variable
write-spec.note: A list of one variable, given by its name.

item-rptena.name: Item
item-rptena.note: "LLN0$RP$urcbWTG01$RptEna": the enable flag of urcbWTG01, the first copy of report control block urcbWTG. RP marks an unbuffered report.

data-list.name: Data
data-list.note: The values to write, one per variable.

true.name: TRUE
true.note: Tag 0x83, a boolean, 1 byte: TRUE. Reports start now.

write-resp.name: Write response
write-resp.note: Tag A5: the answer to a Write, one result per variable.

a-ld.name: Logical device
a-ld.note: WT01WTG: IED name WT01 and instance WTG.

a-ln.name: Logical node
a-ln.note: WMET1: the weather sensors of this turbine. A met mast has its own WMET.

a-hor.name: Horizontal
a-hor.note: Hor. Data object names are built from short words like this one, joined without spaces.

a-wd.name: Wind
a-wd.note: Wd. Other short words: Tmp for temperature, Dir for direction.

a-spd.name: Speed
a-spd.note: Spd. Together: HorWdSpd, the horizontal wind speed.

a-da.name: Data attribute
a-da.note: mag.f: the magnitude, as a float.

facts.standard: IEC 61400-25-2 edition 2 (2015): the model. IEC 61400-25-4: the mappings
facts.between: Park controller, SCADA or owner → turbine, met mast, park
facts.transport: MMS over TCP 102, as in IEC 61850-8-1. OPC UA in IEC 61400-25-41
facts.model: Wind logical nodes: WTUR, WROT, WGEN, WCNV, WMET, WAPC …

tips: Edition 2 (2015) moved the nacelle's wind and weather sensors from WNAC to WMET, and changed several abbreviations. A client written for edition 1 looks in the wrong place.
A value carries no unit. W may be in W or in kW: read units (CF) once after you connect, and keep it.
Turbine makers fill the model differently: optional data objects, instance numbers, data sets. Read the SCL file of each turbine type; do not copy one map to all of them.
Many parks speak IEC 61400-25 toward the operator, but their maker's own protocol toward the turbines. Ask which interface you will get.

anatomy.dataname: A data object name, built from short words

playground.scl: The turbine's configured description (.cid). Open WTG: each part of the turbine is a logical node. WTUR1, WROT1 and WMET1 hold the three values read here. Then open your own file, if you have one.
playground.encoder: MMS sends a float most significant byte first (ABCD). 2350.0 travels as 45 12 E0 00.
